title: WPMS/2878/2017 of SOHAN LAL Vs STATE INFORMATION COMMISSIONER

paras.text:
SL.
No Date
Office Notes,
reports, orders or
proceedings or

Registrar's order
with Signatures
COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPMS No. 2878 of 2017
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Ramji Srivastava, Advocate, for the
petitioner.
Mr. T.S. Phartiyal, Addl. C.S.C. for the State
of Uttarakhand.
The petitioner, who was an Information
Officer has put a challenge to the impugned order
dated 16th October, 2017, as it has been passed by
respondent No.1 / Uttrakhand Information
Commissioner, in Appeal No. 24436 of 2017,
Ashish Kumar Pipaniya Vs. Public Information
Officer / Chief Administrative Officer, Collectorate,
Dehradun, whereby, a direction has been issued for
initiating the criminal proceedings by registering an
FIR against the petitioner under the Prevention of
Corruption Act, 1988, while exercising the
appellate powers under Section 19 (3) of the Right
to Information Act.
When the Writ Petition was argued initially
on 17th November, 2017, the Co-ordinate Bench of
this Court, has issued notices to the respondents, by
virtue of a normal mode, as well as by dasti. The
steps were taken by the petitioner.
The petitioner has filed an affidavit of service
on 27th November 2017, fortifying the fact that the
notices have been served upon the respondents Nos.
1 to 4. On the steps being taken under the normal
process, there is an office report that un-delivered
envelope of service has not yet been received back
by the Registry, hence, it would be deemed that the
respondents had been served with the notices and
also considering the fact that period of service of
notice, which has lapsed as of now in 2022, it
would be deemed that the respondents have been
served with the notices. None has put in
appearance in order to oppose the Writ Petition.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has
argued that on a failure to supply the information

under the provision of Right to Information Act, an
action which has been contemplated to be taken
against the Information Officer, is only envisaged
under Section 20 of the Act, and that could be only
by way of imposition of penalty to be determined
by the competent Authority, as per Section 20 of
the Act. But the ambit of exercise of powers of
Appeal under Section 19 (3), the same cannot be
expanded for by the Appellate Authority, to issue
any direction by directing the authorities to register
an FIR against the Information Officer, though the
petitioner, herein, was not even the designated
Information Officer, and hence, it is argued that the
impugned order dated 16th October, 2017, and the
consequential order dated 30th October, 2017, is in
violation of the provisions contained under Section
20 of the Right to Information Act, as well as it
happens to be an order, which is without
jurisdiction and even outside the ambit and scope of
the exercise of the powers of second appellate
power under Section 19 (3) of the Act, because the
authority thus vested with the powers of an appeal
under the Act, once their action itself are regulated
by the parameters provided under Section 20 of the
Act, the same cannot be expanded by himself
except for imposition of penalty.
In that eventuality, the impugned orders, by
virtue of which, the direction has been issued for
registration of the FIR, against the petitioner under
the Prevention of Corruption Act, is without
jurisdiction and beyond the ambit and scope of the
Act of 2005.
Consequently, the Writ petition is allowed.
The impugned orders are hereby quashed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
Dated 01.04.2022
Shiv
